prerequisites: Manufacturing Processes I from 2nd year, 2nd semester
Manufacturing Processes II from 3rd year, 1st semester

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology, and quality control.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Additive Manufacturing: New Industrial Paradigm.
General aspects of Additive Manufacturing design.
Processing of semi-solid alloys. Main Additive Manufacturing technologies for polymeric and ceramic materials. Main Additive Manufacturing technologies for metallic materials.
Design and modeling for Additive Manufacturing: from concept to manufacturing through CAD/CAM systems. Use of Autodesk Fusion 360 software.
teaching_methods: Resolution of exercises, problems, and practical cases.
assessment_rules: The final grade is the weighted average of the assessment activities, provided each activity has met its minimum score. To pass the course, the weighted average must be at least 5 out of 10. If one or more assessment activities do not meet the minimum score, the final grade for the course will be 4 out of 10. Students who did not present for any assessment activity will receive a 'No presentado' grade. In the extraordinary call, students will only re-take the re-evaluable activities that were not passed, and a minimum 100% attendance to laboratory practicals is required to take the lab practical assessment in both ordinary and extraordinary calls.
